title: Keys: qualifiers, windows and matte finesse

environment.node: 22.23.1 (pinned; the shell default 24.16.0 was not used)

visualAcceptance: none: software measurements only. The owner has not looked at any key or matte view.

delivered.contractDecision: One new effect grade.key 1.0.0 that scopes the grade.* operations after it in its grade run, up to the next grade.key or the end of the run (keyed variants of every grade.* would add about 50 parameters and a version bump to each of 8 effects; a run-level key block has no place in the contract). A CG9 serial node lowers to grade.key + its operators. Spike table and semantics in the decisions file.
delivered.contract: grade.key params: qualifier 0-4 (none, HSL, RGB, luma, sampled OKLab) with HSL names matching comp probe's suggestion; matte finesse (clipBlack/White, denoise, cleanBlack/White, shrinkGrow, blur, inOutRatio, invert); ellipse/rectangle window (centre, size, rotation, roundness, feather, expansion, invert); linear gradient; external matte (matteMode alpha/luma, levels, invert); gain, offset; view 0-3. usesLayerSpace (windows follow the layer or `space`). New effect-definition field optionalLayers: the `matte` slot may stay unbound; validation and both effect contexts honour it.
delivered.colorScience: packages/color-science/src/keys.ts: float64 reference for qualifiers, finesse, gradient, matte levels, key combination, mixing, views and the matte flicker metric; scopes.suggestSampledKey (farthest-point OKLab samples). OKLab now has one home (linearToOklab), used by scopes.
delivered.renderer: float-grade-keys.ts: key spec, float64 frame evaluation (Canvas), GLSL (qualifiers in the fused run shader) and GPU finesse passes (3x3 median, separable square morphology, the blur.gaussian three-box kernel, in/out ratio and invert) on float32 bits in RGBA8 textures. float-grade.ts splits a run into segments at keys; key-free runs keep their exact shader text and Canvas path. Shape windows become a renderer input: a white solid carrying the window as a layer mask (ellipsePath/rectanglePath, rotated) in the key's layer space, drawn by the mask rasterizer. backend.effectStack keeps grade.* effects with inputs inside their run under run-scoped slot names.
delivered.untouchedPixels: A pixel no scoped operation touched (every key 0) leaves the run as its source texel on WebGL2 and its read-back bytes on Canvas, so pixels outside a key are byte-identical on any alpha.
delivered.cli: comp grade key --layer --effect [--frame | --frame-range] [--backend] [--isolate] [--view key|highlight|contrast --still <png>] [--output]: per-frame mean key, keyed fraction and frame-to-frame flicker (still-shift-grade-key-1). comp probe schema 2 adds gradeKey (HSL params) and gradeKeySampled (sampled OKLab params). comp grade bake refuses grade.key.
delivered.previewAndViews: Matte views are the view parameter, so every preview and render shows them; the CLI writes them with comp grade key --view. A key editor in the lab is CG14.
delivered.ce6: Cell catalogue-key-grade (grade.key scoping a grade.primary inside an animated ellipse window, with finesse) and baseline tests/visual/composition-effect-catalogue/darwin-arm64-key-grade-1.json. CG5_LUT_GRADE_EFFECTS pinned to slice(7, 8) so grade.key cannot enter the frozen LUT cell.

qualifierSweeps.float64: keys.ts HSL qualifier equals masks written from the definition (closed-form HSL from HSV, circular hue distance, BT.709 luma, outward Hermite) to 1e-12 on the exact sweep design colors (5 hue-sweep cases x 2 rows x 360 columns, 3 saturation-sweep cases x 6 hues x 256 columns); on the 8-bit fixture bytes within 0.07, the first-order bound from 8-bit input error and softness slope
qualifierSweeps.rendered: 12 gray-key renders (hue and saturation sweeps x 6 qualifier cases) against the analytic mask of each pixel's own HSV: Canvas max 0, WebGL2 max 1 (192 channels at 1, all in the saturation-range case on the saturation sweep)
qualifierSweeps.chromaNodeAudit: research/color-grading-cg6/chroma-node-audit.json: chroma-node evaluateQualifierMask (b804dc0) equals the analytic masks on every chromatic sample (2,256 samples x 5 cases, difference 0) and differs by up to 1 on every neutral sample: it reads gray as hue 0 deg, so a hue range containing red selected every gray. Fixed in the port: a neutral pixel has no hue and is selected by hue only at full width.

keyFromInput.statement: docs/color-grading-cg6-decisions.md (Semantics) and the grade.key contract comment
keyFromInput.test: hue sweep, key on orange (30 +- 20 deg, softness 10) scoping a 180 deg hue rotation: 3,776 pixels keyed and changed; a key taken from the output would differ on 7,552 pixels; rendered output equals the input-keyed reference (Canvas 0, WebGL2 0)

windowEdges.result: 4 windows (ellipse hard; ellipse rotated 25 deg with feather 12 and expansion 4; rounded rectangle rotated -15 deg with feather 6 and expansion -3; rectangle with fractional centre and size): the gray key view equals a white solid layer carrying the same mask path, feather and expansion over black, max difference 0 on Canvas and WebGL2
windowEdges.note: Equal by construction: the renderer draws the window as that layer mask (decision 5). The linear gradient has no edge and is computed directly (deviation).

matteStability.metric: mean absolute frame-to-frame change of the 8-bit gray key (0-1), the fraction of pixels that changed and the largest change, per frame
matteStability.browserGroup: moving-disc.mp4 (48 frames, decoded with ffmpeg to RGBA), background key HSL hue 75 +- 15 (softness 8), saturation >= 0.1. Away from a 3 px band around the disc edge in either frame: raw mean change 0.004262, with finesse (denoise 2, cleanBlack 1, cleanWhite 1, blur 1.5) 0.003210 (-24.7%), both backends equal to 6 decimals; all pixels 0.009300 -> 0.008218 (-11.6%). The changed-pixel fraction does not fall (0.1201 -> 0.1212): the blur spreads small changes over more pixels.
matteStability.cli: comp grade key on a composition of the same clip through the native media path (WebGL2, frames 0:48, 47 flicker values each): raw mean change 0.009599, changed fraction 0.1456; finesse 0.008399 (-12.5%), 0.1423
matteStability.notMeasured: No temporal denoise exists; finesse is spatial only. The metric does not separate legitimate motion from chatter in general (the browser group excludes the disc edge using the clip's stated trajectory).

outsideKeyByteIdentical.result: 66 rows (11 non-view configurations x chart-24, skin-tones, alpha-patches x 2 backends): 1,647,554 pixels with key 0 in the float64 reference, 0 changed against the render without effects (opaque and translucent pixels)

parity.rule: owner decision 3: float64 reference authoritative, WebGL2 within one 8-bit code value, repeat renders byte-identical
parity.configurations: 13 configurations x 3 stills = 39 rows (HSL soft and hard, RGB, luma, sampled OKLab, finesse with in-ratio, finesse with out-ratio and shrink, gain/offset, ellipse window, inverted rounded rectangle with luma, gradient, highlight view, high-contrast view with blur): Canvas max 0 against the reference written from color-science; WebGL2 max 1 (20 channels at 1 in total); every repeated WebGL2 render byte-identical
parity.externalMatte: alpha mode (hidden masked solid: a layer window) and luma mode with inverted levels (hidden image layer): Canvas 0, WebGL2 0
parity.identities: a default grade.key, and a key scoping only a neutral operation, are byte-identical to no effect; a second default key ends the first key's scope (Canvas 0, WebGL2 0)

deviations: The linear gradient window is computed in layer space (0 at gradientStart, 1 at gradientEnd), not produced as mask data: a gradient has no edge for the mask rasterizer. Exact on both backends.
Morphology (clean black/white, shrink/grow) uses a square structuring element (separable, exact); a disc would round corners but costs (2r+1)^2 reads per pixel.

Clean black and clean white are morphological opening and closing of the given radius; denoise is passes of a 3x3 median. Other graders define these controls differently; the definitions are documented, not matched to a product.
Finesse and invert refine the qualifier matte only (with no qualifier they do nothing); windows and the external matte have their own invert; gain and offset apply to the combined key.
A key's view ends the run's processing (later operations in the run are not applied).
